text:
Hockey Wilderness made the case in a headline on Nov. 4: "It's Time To Respect Joel Eriksson Ek As A No. 1 Center." The numbers agree. Eriksson Ek centers Minnesota's top line between Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy, and Quinn Hughes said "we can tilt the ice when they're out there" in Heather Rule's NHL.com recap.

At five on five the Wild take 60% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, nearly 11 points better than without him. He has 17 points in 19 games and an eight-game point streak.

The finishing has not caught up. He has 6 goals on 10.75 expected, shooting 10%. Our numbers say he is due: when a player keeps getting these looks, goals tend to follow. The one caveat is last season, when Evolving-Hockey had his results well ahead of his chances. This year it runs the other way. Watch the goal column over the next month.
headline: Eriksson Ek is a top center short on luck
